name: @kitora/dnd
description: Kitora's drag-and-drop kit: a framework-free engine, DOM sensors and presentation, trees, React bindings, styled presets, an HTML5 bridge and devtools.

exports.name: A11Y_POLICIES
exports.description:
Keyboard and screen-reader drag models; grab-arrow is the
default. `none` turns keyboard dragging off for one surface (its keys belong
to something else, such as Space selecting in a media grid): no pick-up, no
instructions, no drag role description; pointer drags are unchanged.

exports.name: AXES
exports.description: The axis of a list, and of the axis-lock modifier (D79).

exports.name: DIRECTIONS
exports.description: Text direction of a horizontal list; `rtl` mirrors before / after (D48).

exports.name: DRAG_PHASES
exports.description:
Where a drag is. `pending` = pressed but the activation constraint is not met
yet (a click is still possible); `dropping` = an async accept or an async
commit is in flight, so a second drag cannot start.

exports.name: DROP_OPERATIONS
exports.description: What a drop does, like the OS: Alt (or Ctrl) copies, Ctrl+Shift (or Cmd+Alt) links (D60).

exports.name: DROP_POSITIONS
exports.description: Where a move lands relative to its target item. `inside` = combine / reparent (tree, D44).

exports.name: EDGES
exports.description: Rect edges, for the closest-edge hitbox (D55).

exports.name: END_REASONS
exports.description:
Why a drag ended. Only `drop` can carry a `MoveOp`; every other reason sends
the source home (D61, D62).
- `drop`: released over an accepting target
- `escape`: the user cancelled (Escape, or a sensor's cancel gesture)
- `outside`: released over no target
- `invalid`: released over a target whose async accept said no (D57)
- `source-removed`: the dragged item was unregistered mid-drag (D97)
- `pointer-lost`: the sensor lost its pointer (`pointercancel`, lost capture, blur)
- `programmatic`: `engine.cancel()` from app code or a plugin

exports.name: FEEDBACK_MODES
exports.description: What the source shows while dragging; `clone` is the default. Read by the dom layer; the core only carries it.

exports.name: isMember
exports.description: True when `value` is one of `set`'s members; narrows an untyped string (a data attribute, a URL param).
exports.signature: <const T extends string>(set: readonly T[], value: string) => value is T

exports.name: POINTER_KINDS
SORT_STRATEGIES
exports.description:
How a sortable target reacts to a drop (D36). `shift`: the moved item is
inserted before / after the target and the rest shift. `swap`: the moved item
and the target exchange places, nothing else moves.

exports.name: TARGET_KINDS
exports.description:
What a drop target is. `item`: a sortable item (its rect decides before /
after / inside); `container`: a list, column or zone (the move lands at its
end, `MoveOp.to.target` is null).

exports.name: A11yPolicy
exports.description: A keyboard and screen-reader drag model: one of `A11Y_POLICIES`.

exports.name: Axis
exports.description: A list's axis: `x` or `y`.

exports.name: Direction
exports.description: Text direction of a horizontal list: `ltr` or `rtl`.

exports.name: DragPhase
exports.description: Where a drag is: one of `DRAG_PHASES`.

exports.name: DropOperation
exports.description: What a drop does: one of `DROP_OPERATIONS`.

exports.name: DropPosition
exports.description: Where a move lands relative to its target item: one of `DROP_POSITIONS`.

exports.name: Edge
exports.description: A rect edge: one of `EDGES`.

exports.name: EndReason
exports.description: Why a drag ended: one of `END_REASONS`.

exports.name: FeedbackMode
exports.description: What the source shows while dragging: one of `FEEDBACK_MODES`.

exports.name: PointerKind
exports.description: The input driving a drag: one of `POINTER_KINDS`.

exports.name: SortStrategy
exports.description: How a sortable target reacts to a drop: one of `SORT_STRATEGIES`.

exports.name: TargetKind
exports.description: What a drop target is: one of `TARGET_KINDS`.

exports.name: add
exports.description: `a + b`, component-wise.

exports.name: containsPoint
exports.description: True when `p` is inside `r`; the right and bottom edges are exclusive, so adjacent rects never both contain a point.

exports.name: distance
exports.description: Euclidean distance between two points.

exports.name: intersectionArea
exports.description: Area of the overlap of `a` and `b` (0 when they do not touch).

exports.name: ORIGIN
exports.description: The origin, and the "no offset" transform.

exports.name: pointRect
exports.description: A zero-size rect at `p`: the dragged "rect" when the source has no measured box (a file, a scripted drag).

exports.name: rectCenter
exports.description: The centre of `r`.

exports.name: rectCorners
exports.description: The four corners of `r`, top-left clockwise; closest-corners collision compares them pairwise.

exports.name: subtract
exports.description: `a - b`, component-wise.

exports.name: translateRect
exports.description: `r` moved by `offset`.

exports.name: Point
exports.description: A point or a 2D offset.

exports.name: Rect
exports.description: An axis-aligned box, `DOMRect`-compatible on the four fields the core reads.

exports.name: checkActivation
exports.description: The verdict for a press that started at `start`, is now at `current`, and has been held `elapsedMs`.
exports.signature: (constraint: ActivationConstraint, start: Point, current: Point, elapsedMs: number) => ActivationVerdict

exports.name: DEFAULT_ACTIVATION
exports.description:
The defaults: a short delay on touch only, a small distance for
mouse and pen, immediate for the rest. A handle that sets
`touch-action: none` may opt into immediate touch drags per surface.

exports.name: IMMEDIATE
exports.description: Starts on press: keyboard, scripted and native drags have already decided they are drags.

exports.name: MOUSE_ACTIVATION_DISTANCE_PX
exports.description: Mouse and pen: a few px, so a click on a draggable row is not a drag.

exports.name: resolveActivation
exports.description: `DEFAULT_ACTIVATION` with the caller's per-kind overrides on top.

exports.name: TOUCH_ACTIVATION_DELAY_MS
exports.description: Touch: long-press length. Long enough that a swipe scrolls, short enough to feel direct (the field's common 200–300 ms).

exports.name: TOUCH_ACTIVATION_TOLERANCE_PX
exports.description: Touch: finger jitter allowed during the hold before it counts as a scroll.

exports.name: ActivationConstraint
exports.description:
- `distance`: start once the pointer moved `distance` px (0 = on press). A
  click that never moves that far stays a click.
- `delay`: start after holding `delay` ms; moving more than `tolerance` px
  first aborts, so a touch swipe still scrolls the page (long-press).

exports.name: ActivationMap
exports.description: One constraint per pointer kind; a partial map overrides `DEFAULT_ACTIVATION` per kind.

exports.name: ActivationVerdict
exports.description: `pending` = keep waiting; `activate` = start the drag; `abort` = it was a scroll or a click, give the press back.

exports.name: closestCenter
exports.description: Every target, by distance from the dragged box's centre to its centre, nearest first (D52). Never empty while targets exist.

exports.name: closestCorners
exports.description: Every target, by the summed distance of matching corners, nearest first (D52): steadier than centres for items of mixed size.

exports.name: closestEdge
exports.description: The edge of `rect` nearest `point`, among `edges` (D55). Ties go to the earlier edge in `edges`.
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, point: Point, edges: readonly Edge[]) => Edge | null

exports.name: directionBiased
exports.description:
Wraps a detector so a target behind the direction of motion cannot steal the
drag from the current one (D53). While moving down, a hit whose centre is
above the dragged box's centre is dropped unless it is the current target;
same per axis. If that empties the list the base result stands, so the bias
only ever removes flicker, never all targets.

exports.name: MAX_INSIDE_BAND
exports.description: Largest legal `insideBand`: half the box on each side of the middle is the whole box.

exports.name: pointerNear
exports.description:
`pointerWithin`, plus a slack for the gaps between items: targets
within `slack` px of the pointer that are smaller than the innermost target
under it (or any, when it is under none) count first, nearest first. A list with `gap-1` then never drops to "over nothing" while
the pointer crosses between two rows (no flicker of the opened gap), yet a
pointer clearly outside the list still hits nothing, so a drop there still
goes home (D62). The sortable presets use it with the list's gap.

exports.name: pointerWithin
exports.description:
Targets containing the pointer, smallest first (D51, the default). Smallest
first puts the innermost of nested targets ahead, and the value is the area
so a caller can see why.

exports.name: positionInRect
exports.description:
The drop position `point` means on an item target's `rect`. Pure maths: the
fraction along the axis, then the band. Out-of-range bands clamp to [0, 0.5].
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, point: Point, options: PositionOptions) => DropPosition

exports.name: rectIntersection
exports.description:
Targets the dragged box overlaps, by overlap ratio (overlap area / target
target area), largest first (D52). Good for free canvases and grids where the
pointer may sit outside the box being dragged.

exports.name: Collision
exports.description: One hit. `value` is the detector's own score, only meaningful within one detector's result.

exports.name: CollisionDetector
exports.description: A collision strategy: hits ordered best first; empty = over nothing (D54: any function of this shape plugs in).

exports.name: CollisionInput
exports.description: Everything a detector may use.

exports.name: CollisionTarget
exports.description: One candidate target as the detector sees it: an id and its measured rect.

exports.name: PositionOptions
exports.description: How an item target splits its box into before / inside / after.

exports.name: applyModifiers
exports.description: Runs `modifiers` left to right, each on the previous one's output. No modifiers = the input transform.

exports.name: composeModifiers
exports.description: One modifier made of several, for passing a preset pipeline around as a single value.

exports.name: lockAxis
exports.description: Keeps movement on one axis (D79): `"y"` for a vertical list, `"x"` for a tab strip.

exports.name: magneticSnap
exports.description:
Pulls the box onto the nearest snap point when its anchor is within `radius`
(D82), per axis, so it can snap to a vertical guide while moving freely along
it. Outside the radius the offset passes through.

exports.name: restrictToBounds
exports.description:
Keeps the dragged box inside `bounds()` (D80). `bounds` is read on every move
so a scrolling or resizing container stays correct; null = no bounds right
now. A box larger than the bounds is pinned to the bounds' top-left.
Without a source rect the pointer itself is kept inside.

exports.name: SNAP_ANCHORS
exports.description: What part of the dragged box `magneticSnap` aligns with a snap point.

exports.name: snapCenterToCursor
exports.description:
Centres the dragged box under the pointer (D83), ignoring where on the box
the press started. Without a source rect it is a no-op (a point is already
under the pointer).

exports.name: snapToGrid
exports.description: Rounds the offset to multiples of `size` px (D81); `{ x, y }` for different steps per axis. Sizes ≤ 0 leave that axis free.

exports.name: MagneticSnapOptions
exports.description: Options for `magneticSnap`.

exports.name: Modifier
exports.description: One step of the pipeline: returns the new offset (D85: any function of this shape plugs in).

exports.name: ModifierInput
exports.description: What a modifier sees. Only `transform` changes between modifiers; the rest is the drag's fixed context.

exports.name: SnapAnchor
exports.description: Which point of the dragged box `magneticSnap` aligns: one of `SNAP_ANCHORS`.

exports.name: applyMove
exports.description:
The flat list after `op`, when source and destination are the same list.
Pure; returns a new array. A self-drop or an op naming no item of the list
returns a copy unchanged. Swap ops exchange the dragged item and the target.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], op: MoveOp, idOf: (item: T) => string, options?: ApplyMoveOptions<T>) => T[]

exports.name: applyMoveAcross
exports.description:
The layout after `op`, across containers (kanban, D38). Containers the op
does not touch keep their array identity, so a memoised column does not
re-render. Same-container ops delegate to `applyMove`.
exports.signature: <T>(layout: Layout<T>, op: MoveOp, idOf: (item: T) => string, options?: ApplyMoveOptions<T>) => Record<string, readonly T[]>

exports.name: arrayMove
exports.description: `items` with the element at `from` moved to `to` (indices clamped); the classic `arrayMove`.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], from: number, to: number) => T[]

exports.name: arraySwap
exports.description: `items` with the elements at `a` and `b` exchanged; out-of-range indices return a copy unchanged.
exports.signature: <T>(items: readonly T[], a: number, b: number) => T[]

exports.name: isSelfDrop
exports.description: True when the op drops items onto one of themselves: applying it changes nothing.

exports.name: MoveOpError
exports.description: Thrown by the apply helpers for an op they cannot apply honestly (setup errors, not runtime data).

exports.name: ApplyMoveOptions
exports.description: Options for the apply helpers.

exports.name: Layout
exports.description: Containers by id, each an ordered list: a kanban board, a set of lists.

exports.name: MoveOp
exports.description: One drop. `TId` narrows ids for apps with branded id types.

exports.name: BASE_62_DIGITS
exports.description: Base-62 digits in ASCII order, so string order is numeric order.

exports.name: FractionalIndexError
exports.description: Thrown for a key that is not in this format, or for `a >= b`.

exports.name: keyBetween
exports.description:
An order key strictly between `before` and `after` (D91). `null` means "no
neighbour": `keyBetween(null, null)` is the first key of an empty list,
`keyBetween(last, null)` appends, `keyBetween(null, first)` prepends. Throws
`FractionalIndexError` for a malformed key or when `before >= after`.
Deterministic: two peers inserting at the same gap get the same key, so a
CRDT should break ties by appending a peer id or by its own ordering.
exports.signature: (before: string | null, after: string | null) => string

exports.name: keysBetween
exports.description:
`count` ascending keys strictly between `before` and `after`, for a
multi-item drop (D96) or seeding a list. Splits the gap recursively so the
keys stay short instead of chaining one after another.
exports.signature: (before: string | null, after: string | null, count: number) => string[]

exports.name: batchFor
exports.description:
The batch a press on `id` drags: the whole selection (list order) when `id`
is part of it, else `id` alone, which is what every file manager does when
you drag an unselected item next to a selection.

exports.name: EMPTY_SELECTION
exports.description: Nothing selected.

exports.name: nextSelection
exports.description:
The selection after a click on `id` in the list `order`. Ids outside
`order` are dropped first (one list per selection, see the file header); a
range without an anchor in `order` selects `id` alone.
exports.signature: (state: SelectionState, id: string, mode: SelectMode, order: readonly string[]) => SelectionState

exports.name: SELECT_MODES
exports.description: How a click changes the selection: replace it, toggle one item, or extend a range from the anchor.

exports.name: selectModeFor
exports.description: The platform convention: Shift extends a range, Ctrl or Cmd toggles, a plain click replaces.

exports.name: SelectionState
exports.description: A selection: ids in list order, plus the anchor a Shift-click extends from.

props.name: ids
props.description: Selected ids, in list order.

props.name: anchor
props.description: The item a Shift-click extends a range from; null when nothing was clicked yet.

exports.name: SelectMode
exports.description: How a click changes the selection: one of `SELECT_MODES`.

exports.name: createOptimisticState
exports.description: A preview-vs-committed store over any state shape; see `OptimisticState`.

exports.name: CommitOutcome
exports.description: How one proposed op ended.

exports.name: OptimisticOptions
exports.description: Options for `createOptimisticState`.

exports.name: OptimisticState
exports.description: The two-layer store. Every read is a snapshot; `subscribe` fires after each change.

props.name: getView
props.description: What to render: committed state with every in-flight op applied, in proposal order.

props.name: getCommitted
props.description: The confirmed state.

props.name: getPending
props.description: Ops proposed and not yet settled.

props.name: propose
props.description:
Shows `op` at once and runs `commit`. Resolves `committed` when the commit
settles (sync return or a resolved promise), folding the op into the
committed state; resolves `rolled-back` with the error when it throws or
rejects, dropping the op from the view. Never rejects itself.

props.name: setCommitted
props.description:
Replaces the committed state (a server push, a refetch). Pending ops stay
and are re-applied on top, so an in-flight drop does not flicker back.

props.name: subscribe
props.description: Calls `listener` on every change to the shown state; returns the unsubscribe.

exports.name: NO_KEYS
exports.description: No keys held.

exports.name: ContainerDroppableSpec
exports.description: A list, column or zone as a target: a drop lands at its end.

exports.name: DndEngine
exports.description: The engine. Framework-free; the dom and react layers wrap it.

exports.name: DndMonitor
exports.description: Observes every drag (D64). Every callback is optional.

exports.name: DndPlugin
exports.description: Lifecycle extension (D125): devtools, analytics, haptics. `setup` returns its teardown.

exports.name: DragEndEvent
exports.description: How a drag ended.

exports.name: DragSource
exports.description: The drag's source as every callback sees it.

exports.name: DragState
exports.description:
A snapshot of the drag, replaced (never mutated) on every change, so
`getState()` is safe for `useSyncExternalStore`.

props.name: phase
props.description: Where the drag is: idle, pending, dragging or dropping.

props.name: source
props.description: What is being dragged; null when idle.

props.name: origin
props.description: Where the press started.

props.name: pointer
props.description: The pointer's current position; null when idle.

props.name: transform
props.description: The offset after modifiers: what the preview shows.

props.name: over
props.description: The target under the drag; null when over nothing.

props.name: operation
props.description: What a drop would do now: move, copy or link, from the held modifier keys.

props.name: projection
props.description: The op a drop would produce right now (D93: what an optimistic preview renders); null when over nothing.

exports.name: DraggableSpec
exports.description: A draggable as registered by a binding. `TData` is the app's payload (D32).

exports.name: DroppableSpec
exports.description: A drop target as registered by a binding: an item of a sortable list, or a container.

exports.name: EngineOptions
exports.description: `createDndEngine` options. Everything is optional; the defaults are the spec's.

exports.name: ItemDroppableSpec
exports.description: A sortable item as a target: its box splits into before / after (and `inside` with a band).

exports.name: KeyModifiers
exports.description: Modifier keys held during a drag; they pick the drop operation (D60).

exports.name: OverState
exports.description: The target the drag is over.

props.name: id
props.description: The target's id.

props.name: kind
props.description: Whether the target is an item or a container.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the drop lands relative to the target: before, after or inside it.

props.name: rect
props.description: The target's box, measured during this drag.

exports.name: PluginApi
exports.description: What a plugin gets (D125).

exports.name: PressInput
exports.description: What a sensor's `press` takes.

exports.name: ProjectInput
exports.description: What `EngineOptions.project` sees besides the op.

exports.name: Sensor
exports.description: An input source (D12): pointer, keyboard, scripted, or an app's own. Returns its detach.

exports.name: SensorContext
exports.description: The engine as a sensor drives it. Every method is safe to call in any phase; out-of-phase calls are ignored.

exports.name: TargetCandidate
exports.description: A collision candidate with its nesting depth, for `resolveTarget`.

exports.name: createDndEngine
exports.description: The engine; see `DndEngine` and the invariants at the top of this file.

exports.name: operationForKeys
exports.description:
The OS convention (D60): Ctrl+Shift (Windows / Linux) or Cmd+Alt (macOS)
links, Alt or Ctrl copies, nothing moves. Pass `operationFor` to change it.

exports.name: withPinned
exports.description:
A virtualizer's rendered indexes plus the pinned ones, ascending and
without duplicates: what a range extractor returns so a pinned row stays
mounted wherever the window is. Indexes outside `0 … count - 1` are dropped.
exports.signature: (rendered: readonly number[], pinned: readonly number[], count: number) => number[]

exports.name: VirtualPin
exports.description: A virtualized list as the engine sees it; see the file header.

exports.name: VirtualPosition
exports.description: Where an item sits in its virtual list.

exports.name: scriptedSensor
exports.description: A new scripted sensor; pass it in `sensors` (or attach it to `engine.context`).

exports.name: ScriptedDragError
exports.description: Thrown when a script asks for something the engine cannot do; a test failing loudly beats a drag silently not happening.

exports.name: ScriptedDrag
exports.description: A drag in progress; every step returns the same handle so steps chain.

exports.name: ScriptedDragOptions
exports.description: Options for one scripted drag.

exports.name: ScriptedSensor
exports.description: A `Sensor` with a `drag(id)` entry point.

exports.name: createDomDnd
exports.description: The engine wired to the DOM; see the file header.

exports.name: touchActionFor
exports.description: touch-action for a draggable (D139): with a long-press, the page still pans until the drag starts; an immediate touch drag takes the gesture.

exports.name: DomDnd
exports.description: The engine plus its DOM wiring.

exports.name: DomDndOptions
exports.description: `createDomDnd` options: every engine option plus the DOM ones.

exports.name: ElementSpec
exports.description: A spec without `getRect`: the dom layer supplies it from the element. Distributes over the droppable union.

exports.name: animationFrame
exports.description: `requestAnimationFrame` as a `FrameScheduler`.

exports.name: LONG_PRESS_VIBRATE_MS
exports.description: A short buzz when a touch long-press turns into a drag (D11), where the device supports it.

exports.name: pointerSensor
exports.description: The pointer sensor; see the file header. Attaches nothing on a server or without Pointer Events.

exports.name: resolvePress
exports.description:
The draggable a press lands on and the element that bounds it for D18, or
null when the press does not start a drag: no draggable on the path, a
draggable with handles pressed outside them, or an interactive child hit.
exports.signature: (path: readonly Element[], engineId?: string) => { readonly id: string; readonly source: Element; } | null

exports.name: FrameScheduler
exports.description: Schedules one callback before the next paint; returns its cancel. Injected by tests.

exports.name: PointerSensorOptions
exports.description: `pointerSensor` options.

exports.name: CANCEL_KEY
exports.description: The key that cancels.

exports.name: CUT_KEY
exports.description: With Ctrl or Cmd: picks up (cut) and drops (paste) under the clipboard policy (D110).

exports.name: DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_STEP
exports.description: Default px of one nudge in `depth` / `free` mode when the surface sets no `data-dnd-step`.

exports.name: FAST_NUDGE_FACTOR
exports.description: Shift multiplies a `free` nudge by this, for long moves across a canvas.

exports.name: GRAB_KEYS
exports.description: Keys that pick up and drop.

exports.name: keyboardModeOf
exports.description: The arrow mode and nudge size of the surface `el` sits in.
exports.signature: (el: Element) => { readonly mode: KeyboardMode; readonly step: number; }

exports.name: keyboardSensor
exports.description: The keyboard sensor; see the file header.

exports.name: keyboardStops
exports.description:
Leaf drop targets in document order: a target that contains other targets
is stepped through by its children. With `engineId`, only that engine's
targets (a page can hold several engines). With `accepts` (the drag's
`SensorContext.accepts`), only targets that take the held item: a refusing
target is no stop at all (an arrow onto it would be a press that does
nothing, e.g. the outliner row's own group), and a target whose children
all refuse is a leaf again.
exports.signature: (root: Document | Element | ShadowRoot, engineId?: string, accepts?: (targetId: string) => boolean) => string[]

exports.name: PASTE_KEY
exports.description: With Ctrl or Cmd: drops (paste) the held item under the clipboard policy (D110).

exports.name: policyOf
exports.description: The policy of the surface `el` sits in (see the file header).

exports.name: TAB_KEY
exports.description: The key that moves between containers (grab-arrow) or targets (clipboard) while holding.

exports.name: KeyboardSensorOptions
exports.description: `keyboardSensor` options.

exports.name: attachA11y
exports.description:
Announcements, instructions, handle semantics and focus restore for one
dom instance; see the file header. A no-op on a server.

exports.name: createLiveRegion
exports.description: Joins (or creates) `doc`'s polite live region; see {@link LiveRegion}.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DND_MESSAGES
exports.description: The English catalog; see {@link DndMessages}.

exports.name: defineDndMessages
exports.description: `base` with `overrides` on top, key by key (D106).

exports.name: FOCUS_RESTORE_FRAMES
exports.description: Frames the focus restore waits for a moved item to (re)mount before giving up (a commit that remounts it in another list).

exports.name: focusTargetsOf
exports.description: Where keyboard focus lands for draggable `el` (`id`): its handles, else itself (D113).

exports.name: INSTRUCTIONS_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a hidden instructions element; its value is the instruction key (policy, mode, direction).

exports.name: labelOf
exports.description: The spoken name of a draggable or target element (see {@link LABEL_ATTR}).

exports.name: LIVE_REGION_ATTR
exports.description: Marks the kit's live region.

exports.name: MAX_LABEL_LENGTH
exports.description: Longest label read from an element's text, in characters; longer text is cut (a card's whole body is not a name).

exports.name: A11y
exports.description: What `attachA11y` returns.

exports.name: A11yOptions
exports.description: `attachA11y` options.

exports.name: DndInstructionContext
exports.description: What the instructions get.

exports.name: DndMenuMessages
exports.description: The labels of the "Move to…" menu (D109).

exports.name: DndMessageContext
exports.description: What every announcement gets. Positions are 1-based; null when they do not apply (over nothing, a tree).

exports.name: DndMessages
exports.description:
The message catalog (D106). Every key is replaceable; `defineDndMessages`
fills the rest from {@link DEFAULT_DND_MESSAGES}. Functions, not templates,
so a translation controls its own word order and plurals.

exports.name: DndMessagesInput
exports.description: A partial catalog: top-level keys and menu labels, each optional.

exports.name: LiveRegion
exports.description: The kit's live region: one per document, shared by every surface (D105).

exports.name: MOVE_CHOICES
exports.description: The kinds of move a menu offers.

exports.name: moveChoices
exports.description:
The moves item `id` can make right now: up, down, to the top and bottom of
its own list (only those that change something), then the end of every
other list registered on `dnd` that is not disabled. Lists are found from
the registered item targets (their `container`) and container targets.
The item's own list is never offered as "Move to": its home is its item
target's list, else the list its draggable registered in (a kanban card that
is a draggable only, with the column as its one target, is home in that column).
exports.signature: <TData>(dnd: DomDnd<TData>, id: string, labels: DndMenuMessages) => MoveChoice[]

exports.name: runMoveChoice
exports.description:
Runs `choice` for item `id` as a keyboard drag; resolves with the end event,
or null when the drag could not start (busy, disabled, unknown) or the
target is not measurable (it is cancelled then).
exports.signature: <TData>(dnd: DomDnd<TData>, id: string, choice: Pick<MoveChoice, "target" | "position">) => Promise<DragEndEvent<TData> | null>

exports.name: MoveChoice
exports.description: One entry of the menu: its label and where it drops.

exports.name: MoveChoiceKind
exports.description: A kind of move the Move menu offers: one of `MOVE_CHOICES`.

exports.name: createMeasurer
exports.description: The measurer (see the file header). Safe to create on a server: it then never measures.

exports.name: documentScroller
exports.description: The document's scroller: `document.scrollingElement`, else the root element.

exports.name: isScrollContainer
exports.description: True when `el` can scroll its own content (overflow auto / scroll / overlay on either axis).

exports.name: LAZY_MARGIN
exports.description: How far outside the viewport, as a share of its size, an element still counts as "near" and is measured (D101).

exports.name: localOffset
exports.description: A viewport-pixel offset converted to the element's own pixels (D87): divide by its scale.

exports.name: scaleOf
exports.description:
Rendered size over layout size (D87): 1 normally, 0.5 under an ancestor's
`transform: scale(0.5)` or `zoom`. Pointer deltas are viewport pixels, so a
preview positioned in the element's own coordinates divides by this.
Elements without a layout box (SVG) report 1.

exports.name: scrollChain
exports.description:
The scroll containers that move `el` when they scroll, innermost first,
ending with the document scroller unless a fixed ancestor detaches it.
`unstable` is true when a sticky element sits on the way.

exports.name: toRect
exports.description: A plain-object copy of a DOMRect, so cached rects never alias a live object.

exports.name: Measurer
exports.description: The measurer one dom dnd instance owns.

exports.name: MeasurerOptions
exports.description: `createMeasurer` options.

exports.name: canScroll
exports.description:
True when `el` can still scroll on `axis` in direction `dir`. Range-based,
not trial-based, so a sub-pixel step at the start of the ramp does not read
as "stuck" and hand the scroll to an outer scroller. RTL-aware: a
right-to-left scroller's `scrollLeft` runs from 0 down to -max.

exports.name: createAutoScroller
exports.description: The DOM driver; see the file header.

exports.name: DEFAULT_AUTO_SCROLL
exports.description: Defaults: a 56 px band, 1200 px/s at the edge, half a second of ramp, 96 px of overflow.

exports.name: deepElementFromPoint
exports.description: The innermost element at a viewport point, descending into open shadow roots (D145).

exports.name: edgeFraction
exports.description:
Signed depth in [-1, 1] of `pos` in the start (-) or end (+) band of the
span `[start, start + size)`: 0 outside the bands, growing quadratically
towards the edge, ±1 at or past the edge up to `overflow` px beyond it, 0
further out.
exports.signature: (pos: number, start: number, size: number, options: Pick<AutoScrollOptions, "threshold" | "overflow">) => number

exports.name: IDLE_AXIS
exports.description: Not scrolling.

exports.name: scrollAncestors
exports.description: Scroll containers from `el` outwards (D67), not including the document scroller.

exports.name: stepAxis
exports.description:
The next state and the speed (px per second, signed) for one axis.
Hysteresis (D69): the direction never flips in one step; a fraction of the
opposite sign first returns to idle, and the new direction ramps up from
zero, so a pointer held still at an edge never makes a scroller shake.
exports.signature: (prev: AxisState, fraction: number, now: number, options: Pick<AutoScrollOptions, "maxSpeed" | "rampMs">) => { readonly state: AxisState; readonly speed: number; }

exports.name: AutoScroller
exports.description: The running auto-scroller of one drag.

exports.name: AutoScrollerSource
exports.description: What the driver needs from its host each frame.

exports.name: AutoScrollOptions
exports.description: Tuning. Every field is optional where it is taken; these are the defaults.

exports.name: AxisState
exports.description: Per scroller and axis: the direction it is scrolling and when that started.

props.name: dir
props.description: Scroll direction on this axis: -1 back, 0 still, 1 forward.

props.name: since
props.description: When scrolling in `dir` started, as a timestamp in ms.

exports.name: INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR
exports.description:
Elements that own their own pointer behaviour. `button` is here because a
button inside a card (delete, menu) must click, not drag; a draggable that
is itself a button is excluded by the boundary rule above.

exports.name: pressHitsInteractive
exports.description:
True when a press whose composed path is `path` (innermost first) hits an
interactive element strictly inside `boundary` (the draggable or its handle).
Elements outside the boundary never count.

exports.name: HONEYPOT_ATTR
exports.description: Marks the honey-pot element, for tests and for app CSS that must ignore it.

exports.name: HONEYPOT_TTL_MS
exports.description: The honey pot never outlives this, even without input.

exports.name: installHoneypot
exports.description: Places the honey pot at `point`; returns its removal (also run on the next move, press or timeout).

exports.name: ensureBaseStyle
exports.description: Adds the base rules to `doc` once; a no-op on a server.

exports.name: ensurePresentationStyle
exports.description: Adds the presentation defaults to `doc` once; a no-op on a server.

exports.name: INDICATOR_ATTR
exports.description: Marks the drop indicator element; its `data-position` is the drop position.

exports.name: LANDED_ATTR
exports.description: Set on an item for a moment after it lands (D74): `motion` animates a highlight, `static` shows it without motion.

exports.name: OVER_ATTR
exports.description: Set on the target element the drag is over; its value is the drop position.

exports.name: PLACEHOLDER_ATTR
exports.description: Set on the source while a clone preview stands in for it (D22): it stays in the list as the placeholder. Value: the feedback mode.

exports.name: PLACEHOLDER_AWAY
exports.description: `PLACEHOLDER_ATTR`'s value while a clone drag is over another list (D38): the placeholder is hidden so its list can close up.

exports.name: PRESSING_ATTR
exports.description: Set on a touch source during the long-press hold (D11): style it to show the hold is registering.

exports.name: PREVIEW_ATTR
exports.description: Marks the preview wrapper; its value is the content kind (`clone` | `custom`). Declared here so the stylesheet and `preview.ts` share it.

exports.name: ROOT_STATE_ATTR
exports.description: Set on the root element while a press or drag is live (`pending` | `dragging`).

exports.name: SHIFTING_ATTR
exports.description: Set on items that are shifting to make room (D71); the presentation style gives them a `translate` transition.

exports.name: SOURCE_STATE_ATTR
exports.description: Set on the source element while it is pressed or dragged: `pending` | `dragging`.

exports.name: VIEW_TRANSITION_CLASS
exports.description: The `view-transition-class` the commit animation gives its elements, so the timing rules below touch no other transition on the page.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DROP_DURATION_MS
exports.description: Drop animation length when `--dnd-drop-duration` is unset, in ms; shorter than a shift so the drop feels like it lands.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DURATION_MS
exports.description: Shift and commit animation length when `--dnd-duration` is unset, in ms.

exports.name: DND_EASINGS
exports.description:
Easing presets. `spring` is a CSS `linear()` curve sampled from a damped
spring (stiffness 170, damping 18, mass 1, 0.6 s): it overshoots by 5%
and settles, with no JavaScript physics per frame. Pair it with a
`--dnd-duration` near 600ms, the length it was sampled over.

exports.name: MOTION_POLICIES
exports.description:
How a surface treats motion: `auto` follows `prefers-reduced-motion`,
`never` turns every animation off (tests, a "no animation" setting),
`always` ignores the media query (only for a demo that compares both).

exports.name: MOTION_VARS
exports.description: The custom properties read by `motionTiming`; set them on any ancestor of the list (or `:root`).

exports.name: motionAllowed
exports.description: The one question every animation asks first.

exports.name: motionTiming
exports.description: The timing for animations on `el`, read from the custom properties it inherits (D73), else the defaults.

exports.name: parseTime
exports.description: Parses a CSS time (`200ms`, `0.2s`, a bare number = ms); NaN for anything else.

exports.name: prefersReducedMotion
exports.description: True when the user asked for reduced motion (D77); false on a server or where `matchMedia` is missing.

exports.name: MotionPolicy
exports.description: How a surface treats motion: one of `MOTION_POLICIES`.

exports.name: MotionTiming
exports.description: Resolved timing for one animation.

exports.name: hasMoveBefore
exports.description: Whether this browser keeps node state across a reorder.

exports.name: MOVE_METHODS
exports.description: How a node was moved: the closed set `moveNode` reports, so a demo or test can show which path ran.

exports.name: moveNode
exports.description:
Moves `node` before `before` (null = append) inside `parent` and returns the
method used. Focus inside `node` is kept: free with moveBefore, restored
(without scrolling) after an insertBefore (D112).
exports.signature: (parent: Node, node: Element, before: Node | null, options?: MoveNodeOptions) => MoveMethod

exports.name: reorderChildren
exports.description:
Reorders `parent`'s element children to match `order` (each element must be
a child of `parent`), moving only the nodes that are out of place; returns
the method of the last move, or null when nothing moved.
exports.signature: (parent: Element, order: readonly Element[], options?: MoveNodeOptions) => MoveMethod | null

exports.name: MoveMethod
exports.description: How `moveNode` moved a node: one of `MOVE_METHODS`.

exports.name: MoveNodeOptions
exports.description: `moveNode` options.

exports.name: animateCommit
exports.description:
Runs `mutate` and animates `elements` (read before and after) from their old
layout to the new one; see the file header for the three paths. With View
Transitions the mutation runs inside the transition's update callback, a
task later; on the other paths it runs before this function returns.
exports.signature: (elements: () => Iterable<Element>, mutate: () => void, options?: CommitOptions) => CommitResult

exports.name: captureLayout
exports.description: Records the on-screen elements' boxes (FLIP's First); off-screen ones are left out so they never animate.

exports.name: COMMIT_ANIMATIONS
exports.description: Which path `animateCommit` took: the closed set, for demos and tests.

exports.name: flipOffset
exports.description: The FLIP offset from where an element was to where it is now.

exports.name: playFlip
exports.description:
Animates every element in `snapshot` that is still connected from its old
box to its current one (Invert, Play); returns the running animations.
Animations are WAAPI, so they leave no inline transform behind when they finish.

exports.name: supportsViewTransitions
exports.description: True when the document can run a View Transition (D75); false on a server, in jsdom and in older browsers.

exports.name: CommitAnimation
exports.description: Which path `animateCommit` took: one of `COMMIT_ANIMATIONS`.

exports.name: CommitOptions
exports.description: `animateCommit` options.

exports.name: CommitResult
exports.description: What `animateCommit` returns: the path it took and a promise that settles when the animation is over.

exports.name: FlipOptions
exports.description: FLIP options.

exports.name: LayoutSnapshot
exports.description: Boxes recorded before a mutation (FLIP's First).

exports.name: insertionSlot
exports.description:
Where a foreign item dropped by `op` lands in `items` (a list it did not
start in): the slot before or after its target, or null when the op names
no item of this list (a drop on the column itself goes to its end, which
moves nobody) or combines (`inside`).
exports.signature: (items: readonly ShiftItem[], op: MoveOp | null) => number | null

exports.name: insertOffsets
exports.description:
A line list a foreign item is ENTERING at `slot` (kanban, D38; palette copy,
D39): the items from `slot` on make room by the incoming item's `size` plus
the list's own gap, so variable sizes still line up (D37).
exports.signature: (items: readonly ShiftItem[], slot: number, size: number, axis: Axis) => Map<string, Point>

exports.name: isWrapping
exports.description:
True when the items wrap onto more than one row AND more than one column (a
CSS grid or a wrapping flex row, D35). A vertical list shares its lefts, a
horizontal one its tops; only a grid has both kinds of break, and there the
per-axis model is wrong, so the slot model (`slotOffsets`) takes over.

exports.name: itemGap
exports.description: The space between consecutive items along `axis`; 0 for a list of one.

exports.name: projectedIndex
exports.description:
The index the source would land at in its own list for `op` (the same rule
as `applyMove`: positions count without the source), or null when `op`
leaves this list, names a target that is not in it, or is a combine (`inside`).
exports.signature: (items: readonly ShiftItem[], sourceId: string, op: MoveOp | null) => number | null

exports.name: removeOffsets
exports.description:
A line list the source LEFT (kanban, D38): the items after `from` close the
hole by the source's pitch. The source itself gets no entry (the presenter
hides its placeholder instead).
exports.signature: (items: readonly ShiftItem[], from: number, axis: Axis) => Map<string, Point>

exports.name: shiftOffsets
exports.description:
Offsets per item id for the source at `from` landing at `to`; ids without
an entry stay put. The source's own entry is where its box moves to (the
placeholder's spot in `clone` feedback).
exports.signature: (items: readonly ShiftItem[], from: number, to: number, axis: Axis) => Map<string, Point>

exports.name: slotOffsets
exports.description:
The slot model (wrapping grids, D35): `next` is the order the slots will
hold, as ids; every item of `items` that lands in another slot moves to that
slot's box. It covers a reorder (`next` a permutation), the source leaving
(`next` without it) and a foreign item entering (`next` with an id that is
not in `items`, which gets no entry). Uniform cells are assumed, as in any
grid that wraps.
exports.signature: (items: readonly ShiftItem[], next: readonly string[]) => Map<string, Point>

exports.name: swapOffsets
exports.description:
Swap mode (D36): the target takes the source's box and the source's
placeholder takes the target's; nothing else moves. Works across lists
because both boxes are viewport rects.

exports.name: ShiftItem
exports.description: An item of the list being sorted, in index order.

exports.name: clonePreview
exports.description:
A copy of `el` that is safe to show twice: no ids (duplicates break labels
and axe), no kit markers, iframes and media replaced by empty boxes of the
same size, hidden from assistive tech and inert.

exports.name: createPreview
exports.description: Creates the preview on top of `source`'s box `origin`; see the file header.
exports.signature: <TSource>(source: Element, origin: Rect, content: PreviewContent<TSource>, options?: PreviewOptions) => Preview

exports.name: PREVIEW_FALLBACK_Z
exports.description: The fallback stacking value when the Popover API is missing: above the overlay kit's tooltip band.

exports.name: supportsPopover
exports.description: True when the Popover API is available, so the preview can join the top layer (D131).

exports.name: Preview
exports.description: A live preview.

exports.name: PreviewContent
exports.description: What a preview shows.

exports.name: PreviewOptions
exports.description: `createPreview` options.

exports.name: PreviewRenderer
exports.description:
An app-rendered preview (D19): draw into `container` (React: a portal into
it), return a cleanup. The container is already positioned on the source's box.

exports.name: createDropIndicator
exports.description: Creates the (hidden) indicator; see the file header.

exports.name: INDICATOR_METHODS
exports.description: How an indicator was placed: the closed set, for demos and tests.

exports.name: INDICATOR_THICKNESS
exports.description: Line thickness in px; the line is centred on the edge.

exports.name: indicatorBox
exports.description: The line's box for the measured path: the target edge for `before` / `after` (mirrored under RTL on x), the whole box for `inside`.
exports.signature: (rect: Rect, position: DropPosition, axis: Axis, direction: Direction) => Rect

exports.name: supportsAnchorPositioning
exports.description: True when CSS Anchor Positioning is available (feature detection, D132).

exports.name: DropIndicatorHandle
exports.description: The drop indicator; `show` and `hide` are cheap enough to call on every published drag state.

exports.name: DropIndicatorOptions
exports.description: `createDropIndicator` options.

exports.name: IndicatorMethod
exports.description: How an indicator was placed: one of `INDICATOR_METHODS`.

exports.name: IndicatorTarget
exports.description: Where the indicator should be: a target, how the drop relates to it, and the target's list geometry.

exports.name: STACK_BADGE_ATTR
exports.description: Marks the count badge, for styling and tests.

exports.name: STACK_PREVIEW_MAX
exports.description: How many items the stack draws; the badge still counts all of them.

exports.name: STACK_PREVIEW_STEP_PX
exports.description: Offset between two cards of the stack, px.

exports.name: stackedPreview
exports.description:
A preview renderer that stacks the batch's items (the pressed one on top)
and badges the count; pass it as `presentation.renderPreview`.

exports.name: StackedPreviewOptions
exports.description: `stackedPreview` options.

exports.name: attachPresentation
exports.description: Presents drags on `dnd`; see the file header. Returns the handle whose `destroy` detaches it.

exports.name: FLASH_MS
exports.description: How long the landing highlight stays (D74), in ms; the CSS animation reads `--dnd-flash-duration` and should match.

exports.name: INDICATOR_KINDS
exports.description: How the drop slot is shown: siblings make room, a line on the target, or nothing.

exports.name: IndicatorKind
exports.description: How the drop slot is shown: one of `INDICATOR_KINDS`.

exports.name: Presentation
exports.description: The live presentation; mostly for demos and tests.

exports.name: PresentationOptions
exports.description: `attachPresentation` options; every field is optional (feedback defaults to `clone`).

exports.name: A11Y_POLICY_ATTR
exports.description:
Picks the keyboard / screen-reader model for every draggable under it
(D108–D110): `grab-arrow` (the default), `menu` (no keyboard
pick-up; a "Move to…" menu per item does the moving) or `clipboard`
(Tab-to-target: pick up, Tab / Shift+Tab between drop targets, drop).
Read from the nearest ancestor, so one page can mix surfaces.

exports.name: composedParent
exports.description:
The parent of `node` across shadow boundaries (D145): a slotted node's slot,
else its parent element, else the host of the shadow root it sits in.

exports.name: DRAGGABLE_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a registered draggable; its value is the draggable id. The pointer and keyboard sensors find sources by it.

exports.name: draggableById
exports.description:
The registered draggable element whose id is `id` in `doc`, without building
a selector from the id (ids may hold any character); with `engineId`, only
one that engine owns.
exports.signature: (doc: Document, id: string, engineId?: string) => Element | null

exports.name: DROPPABLE_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a registered drop target; its value is the target id.

exports.name: eventElements
exports.description: Elements on an event's composed path, innermost first, so a press inside an open shadow root still finds its draggable (D145).

exports.name: HANDLE_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a handle: when a draggable contains one, only a press on a handle starts a drag (D16 builds on it).

exports.name: HANDLE_FOR_ATTR
exports.description:
An external handle (D17): an element anywhere in the document, outside the
draggable, whose value is the id of the draggable a press on it drags (a
toolbar grip, a row number in another column).

exports.name: hasDom
exports.description: True when a DOM exists (a browser or jsdom), false on a server or in a worker.

exports.name: isRtl
exports.description:
Whether `el` lays out right-to-left, for direction-aware maths. The
document's directionality (`dir` attributes, through `:dir(rtl)`) answers
where the selector exists, so a CSS-only `direction: rtl` without `dir` is
not seen there (use `dir`, as HTML asks); elsewhere the computed `direction`,
and an engine that does not compute it (jsdom) the nearest `dir` attribute.

exports.name: isVisibleTarget
exports.description:
True when `el` can take a keyboard drop (D152): in the document, not inside
`hidden` or `inert`, rendered (`checkVisibility` where the engine has it)
and with a box. A collapsed folder's children and a closed column fail it.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_MODE_ATTR
exports.description:
What the arrow keys do during a keyboard drag of an item under it:
`step` (the default) steps through the drop targets; `depth` keeps the
vertical arrows on the targets and turns the horizontal ones into a nudge of
one {@link KEYBOARD_STEP_ATTR} (a tree's indent: outdent / indent); `free`
makes every arrow a nudge in two dimensions (a canvas, which has one target).

exports.name: KEYBOARD_MODES
exports.description: The keyboard modes {@link KEYBOARD_MODE_ATTR} takes.

exports.name: KEYBOARD_STEP_ATTR
exports.description: The px one nudge moves in `depth` and `free` keyboard modes; read beside {@link KEYBOARD_MODE_ATTR}.

exports.name: LABEL_ATTR
exports.description:
The name announcements use for a draggable or a target (D105). Optional:
without it the kit reads `aria-label`, then the element's text. Set it when
the visible text is not a good spoken name ("Card 3" instead of a whole
card's body).

exports.name: NO_DRAG_ATTR
exports.description: Opt-out marker: a press inside an element carrying it never starts a drag (D18), whatever the element is.

exports.name: ownedBy
exports.description: True when `el` belongs to the engine `engineId` (an untagged element, from a binding that does not tag, counts as anyone's).

exports.name: OWNER_ATTR
exports.description:
Set on a registered draggable or drop target to the `engineId` of the engine that owns it.
Sensors listen on the whole document, and two engines on one page may both
have an item "Item 1"; a sensor presses only elements its engine owns.

exports.name: pointerKindOf
exports.description: The pointer kind for a `PointerEvent.pointerType` (D4: pen is its own kind). An unknown or empty type counts as mouse.

exports.name: supportsPointerEvents
exports.description: True when the browser has Pointer Events (D129); without them the pointer sensor attaches nothing rather than half-working.

exports.name: KeyboardMode
exports.description: A keyboard mode {@link KEYBOARD_MODE_ATTR} takes: one of `KEYBOARD_MODES`.

exports.name: buildTree
exports.description:
The nested tree of `rows` (the inverse of `flattenTree` with every node
expanded; also what a server's `parent_id` rows build into). Children keep
their order in `rows`; a row whose parent is missing becomes a root, so a
partial page of rows never loses a node.

exports.name: descendantIds
exports.description: Every id below `node` (not `node` itself), in pre-order.

exports.name: findNode
exports.description: The node `id`, or undefined.
exports.signature: <T>(nodes: readonly TreeNode<T>[], id: string) => TreeNode<T> | undefined

exports.name: flattenTree
exports.description:
The rows of `nodes` in display order (pre-order). With `isExpanded`, a node
it answers false for hides its descendants; without it every node is shown.
exports.signature: <T>(nodes: readonly TreeNode<T>[], isExpanded?: (id: string) => boolean) => FlatTreeNode<T>[]

exports.name: isDescendant
exports.description: True when `id` sits strictly below `ancestor` in `nodes`.
exports.signature: <T>(nodes: readonly TreeNode<T>[], ancestor: string, id: string) => boolean

exports.name: topmostIds
exports.description:
`ids` without the ones whose ancestor is also in `ids`, in pre-order: moving
a folder moves its contents, so a selected child of a selected folder is not
moved a second time (D96 on a tree).
exports.signature: <T>(nodes: readonly TreeNode<T>[], ids: readonly string[]) => string[]

exports.name: FlatTreeNode
exports.description: One visible row of a flattened tree.

exports.name: TreeNode
exports.description: One node: an id unique across the whole tree, the app's payload, and its children in order.

exports.name: TreeRow
exports.description: A row of a flat tree as `buildTree` reads it: id, payload and parent, in display order.

exports.name: applyTreeMove
exports.description:
The tree after `op`; pure, the branches the op does not touch keep their
identity (a memoised row does not re-render), and a move that changes
nothing returns `nodes` itself. Selected children of a
selected folder move with it, once (`topmostIds`). A self-drop, or an op
naming no node of the tree, returns `nodes` unchanged. A target that no
longer exists means the end of the root list (D49). Throws `MoveOpError`
for a move into a moved node's own subtree, and for `copy` / `link` without
`options.duplicate`.
exports.signature: <T>(nodes: readonly TreeNode<T>[], op: MoveOp, options?: ApplyTreeMoveOptions<T>) => readonly TreeNode<T>[]

exports.name: isDropIntoDescendant
exports.description: True when `op` would put a moved node inside its own subtree (a refused drop). A self-drop is not one: it changes nothing.

exports.name: ApplyTreeMoveOptions
exports.description: Options for `applyTreeMove`; `duplicate` makes the new subtree of a `copy` / `link` drop.

exports.name: DEFAULT_TREE_INDENT
exports.description: Default indent per level, px: the preset's row padding step and the offset that changes depth by one.

exports.name: projectTreeDrop
exports.description:
The tree drop for a hit row and a horizontal offset; null when the hit row
is inside a dragged subtree (a node cannot move into itself, D41) or unknown.
See the file header for the depth rule.

exports.name: withTreeDestination
exports.description: `op` with its destination replaced by the projection's; the engine's `project` hook returns this.

exports.name: TreeProjection
exports.description: A projected tree drop.

exports.name: TreeProjectionInput
exports.description: What `projectTreeDrop` reads.

exports.name: SPRING_DWELL_MS
exports.description: Default dwell before a hovered collapsed node opens, ms (Finder and VS Code use roughly half a second to a second).

exports.name: springLoad
exports.description: The spring-loading plugin; pass it in `plugins` (engine, `createDomDnd` or `DndProvider`).

exports.name: SpringLoadOptions
exports.description: `springLoad` options.

exports.name: SpringTimer
exports.description: Schedules `run` after `ms` and returns its cancel; tests pass a manual one.

exports.name: useA11y
exports.description:
The accessibility layer (announcements, instructions, handle semantics, focus
restore; `attachA11y`) on a `useDomDnd` instance. Attached once per instance
and re-attached only when `policy`, `announce` or `restoreFocus` change; the
catalog is read at attach (give the provider a new `key` to switch
language), `label` and `onAnnounce` through a ref. `false` attaches nothing.
exports.signature: <TData>(dnd: DomDnd<TData> | null, options?: A11yOptions | false) => A11y | null

exports.description: One `DataTransferItem` as visible during a drag. `type` is "" when the browser does not know it (Safari often, on dragenter).

exports.name: NativeKind
exports.description: A data kind the HTML5 bridge brings in: one of `NATIVE_KINDS`.

exports.name: NativePayload
exports.description: The dropped data, read in the `drop` event. Absent kinds are empty, never undefined.

exports.name: RejectedFile
exports.description: A file `filterPayload` refused, and why.

exports.name: ensureNativeStyle
exports.description: Adds the bridge's default rule to `doc` once; a no-op on a server.

exports.name: NATIVE_ACTIVE_ATTR
exports.description: On the root element while a bridge drag is live: `inbound` or `outbound`. Style "files are being dragged over the page" from it.

exports.name: NATIVE_SOURCE_ATTR
exports.description: On an element registered with `nativeDraggable`; its value is the draggable id.

exports.name: NATIVE_TARGET_ATTR
exports.description: On the target under a native drag: `accept` (the engine is over it) or `reject` (it refused the drag).
